transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Nice to meet you too. I'm here because... well, after I eat too much, I keep going to the bathroom and making myself throw up. I do it so I won't gain weight, but it's gotten to the point where I'm honestly scared I can't stop doing it anymore.
Before you make yourself vomit, do you usually eat an unusually large amount of food?

Yeah, I do. Usually it happens at night. After everyone's gone quiet, I'll just stand in the kitchen and eat. I'll go through leftovers, cereal, chips, ice cream... whatever's there, really. I eat way past a normal meal, just keeping at it until half the pantry looks picked over.
Are you currently at a significantly low body weight for your height?
No, not at all. I'm... well, I'm just an average weight, really. Maybe even a little on the heavier side, honestly. I definitely don't look too skinny or anything like that.
When that eating happens, do you feel like you can't stop or control how much you're eating?

Yeah, exactly. Once I start on those nights, it's like... I just can't stop. My hands just keep grabbing food, opening packages, even while I'm standing there telling myself, 'Lucy, knock it off, you don't need this.' But I just keep eating. I don't feel like I'm back in charge of myself until it's already done and I'm stuffed.

latest_inference.note: Recurrent objectively large binge episodes with loss of control, followed by self-induced vomiting to avoid weight gain, in the absence of significantly low body weight, rules out anorexia nervosa binge-purge type and supports bulimia nervosa over other eating disorders.
